Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

{"visible_record": {"initial_information_actually_supplied": "A retrospective multicentre series records 18 treated attacks in 17 people with MOGAD or AQP4-positive NMOSD. IL-6 receptor blockade began within one month of attack nadir. Thirteen attacks were treated as acute escalation after inadequate earlier therapy; five represented early initiation of maintenance treatment.
The authors report an EDSS improvement before IL-6 blockade, from a nadir median of 5.0 to a pre-blockade median of 3.5 (P=.001), and a further decrease to 2.0 at three months (P=.03 versus pre-blockade). These are the reported comparison summaries; the packet does not establish the participant subset for every paired comparison. There is no concurrent untreated control group. Earlier corticosteroids/plasma exchange and spontaneous recovery can affect the course.", "original_task": "Audience: a clinician. Use 180–240 words in English. Explain what the sequence supports and what it leaves unresolved about an acute rescue effect. Address attacks versus patients, the two treatment intentions, the improvement already present before blockade, and why the reported P values do not alone identify a causal effect. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "**Interpreting the IL-6 blockade series**

The reported sequence is compatible with, but does not demonstrate, an acute rescue effect. The unit of analysis is attacks (18) in 17 patients, so some patients contribute more than once; paired comparisons may therefore mix attacks and patients, and the packet does not specify which participants underlie each P value.

Two distinct intentions are pooled: 13 attacks were acute escalations after inadequate earlier therapy, and five were early initiation of maintenance treatment. These differ mechanistically and prognostically—maintenance initiation aims to prevent relapses, not to reverse the current attack—so combining them weakens inference about rescue specifically.

Crucially, substantial improvement occurred before IL-6 blockade (median EDSS 5.0 to 3.5, P=.001). That change reflects earlier corticosteroids/plasma exchange and spontaneous recovery, not blockade. The further decline to 2.0 (P=.03 versus pre-blockade) is consistent with continued natural recovery or delayed treatment effects, and without a concurrent untreated control group, natural history cannot be separated from drug effect.

The P values describe statistical significance of within-group changes; they do not establish causality because confounding by prior therapy, spontaneous improvement, regression to the mean, and selection of treatment timing are unaddressed.
